newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish central bank buys lira for dollars - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish central bank buys lira for dollars - bankers.

text.p: Turkey's central bank began buying lira for dollars in early afternoon on Monday to support the local currency amid increased concerns over the future of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government, bankers said.
They said the central bank began buying lira at 135,300-135,310 versus the dollar, after which the lira firmed to 135,250 against the dollar.

The difference between the central bank's key dollar rate for compulsory foreign currency transfers and the banks' dollar bids dropped to 0.2 percent after the central bank's sales from previous 0.3, bankers said.
The key dollar rate was 134,900 lira.
Bankers said there was no significant demand for the U.S. currency as banks were cautious after the central bank's dollar interventions on Thursday and Friday to support the lira.

Turkish markets remain uneasy amid persisting concerns over the future of the Islamist-led coalition after the resignations of two conservative ministers and a critical National Security Council (NSC) meeting at the weekend.
Political fears haunted the bond market most, bankers said, leading to weak trade volume.
"The negative political situation and the high funding cost caused by liquidity shortage are effective. Players prefer to keep cash rather than buy paper," said one banker.
